caption: The drawing depicts the inner mechanism of a wooden clock, primarily rectangular in shape and colored in various shades of brown to represent wood grain. The clock mechanism includes several visible gears; one large, toothed, circular gear is partially within the main wooden section, accompanied by a smaller yellow-green toothed gear above it. Several metal pins and axles, rendered in metallic gray, are fixed through the wood. Hanging from the mechanism are three cords: the left and right cords are attached to cylindrical, stone-like weights with a worn, partially rusted brown coloration; the middle cord is attached to a large, round, gold medallion with an embossed decorative pattern and a small, gold, rectangular object fastened just above it. The objects hang downward freely, with shadows indicating three-dimensionality. The background is a plain, light beige color. The artist's signature and date, "Lemuel D. Stock 1940," appear in the lower right corner.
title: Mechanism of Eli Terry Clock
